- Model consistently underestimates true price spikes, especially after sentiment shifts to positive (sentiment > 0.5) — adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for such periods.
- After a sharp price spike (true > 75), model fails to sustain momentum; forecast flattens or declines prematurely — add 2–5% buffer to avoid premature correction.
- When sentiment is low (sentiment < 0.3), model overestimates mean-reversion, leading to premature downward drift — increase forecast by 1–2% to counteract mean-reversion bias.
- Model exhibits lag in reacting to sentiment changes — if sentiment rises sharply, delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days to avoid overreacting.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate volatility in high-sentiment periods — increase forecast slope by 0.1–0.3 per day during sentiment > 0.6.
- Overshoot correction: if model forecast exceeds true outcome by > 2% for 3 consecutive days, reduce slope by 0.05–0.1 per day to avoid overcorrection.
